implementation_barriers.barrier: Lack of staff education and awareness, and neglected CAS maintenance

There may be many reasons for 
air leakages such as the lack of education levels of the staff, inadequate 
awareness level, neglecting CAS maintenances, gaps and cracks occur­
ring between installation and fitting elements as a result of expansion/ 
contraction due to seasonal hot-cold differences.

implementation_barriers.evidence_quote:

count because they thought the air was cheap.

implementation_barriers.barrier: Engineers address CAS only reactively when the compressor fails
implementation_barriers.evidence_quote:
In some facilities, engineers act about the CAS only when there is a 
problem with the compressor.

reviewer_notes: Paper studies 44 industrial facilities across 10 sectors (defined multi-site population) with a detailed numeric demonstration on one steel production facility; treated as a single multi-site application A1. Five models extracted: SEC (M1, reference intensity ratio, no numeric value computed), SES (M2), SCAS (M3) and SLS (M4) are new specific-saving intensity ratios demonstrated numerically on the steel facility; M5 is the empirical quadratic dB-to-air-flow-rate correlation (Equation 2), which is not an energy quantity itself but is the only fitted statistical model in the paper (R2=0.99, Table 1) and feeds the energy/CO2 calculations. Energy vectors for CAS savings (M3/M4) marked electricity by inference (compressor energy). Denominators for M2/M3/M4 marked production mass because the demonstration is reported in TOE per ton of steel, though the indicators are defined generically per amount of product.
